name: Martini
description: Gin and dry vermouth stirred cold—aromatic, crisp, and endlessly tunable.
history: The Martini evolved from 19th-century gin cocktails into the dry, elegant template known today. Ratios are personal; clarity and coldness are not.
whyItWorks: Vermouth softens gin’s botanicals and adds a quiet herbal line. Dilution and temperature are half the drink.
steps: Add gin, dry vermouth, and optional orange bitters to a mixing glass with ice.
Stir until icy cold, about 30 seconds.
Express a lemon peel over the surface, or garnish with an olive for a savory finish.
techniqueNotes: This build is dry (5:1). Increase vermouth toward 1 oz for a wetter Martini.
Stir rather than shake for a clearer, silkier texture.

recommendedBottles.rationale: Gunpowder tea and green spice make a distinctive, modern Martini.
Clean Italian juniper profile—bright and classic.

variations.name: Wet Martini
variations.notes: Use 2 oz gin and 1 oz dry vermouth.
